name: MAST
summary: MAST is a large liquid-argon space gamma-ray-telescope concept for a proposed space deployment, with no formally established mission orbit. Here MAST does not refer to other ground telescopes or databases with the same name.
physics_targets: Gamma rays from dark-matter annihilation / decay
detection_principle: A large liquid-argon TPC acts as the gamma-conversion medium and records the tracks and ionization energy of charged secondaries, extending space gamma-ray observations through a large effective area and improved angular resolution.

science_scope: Searches cosmic gamma-ray, antiparticle or neutrino spectra, directions and fluxes for indirect signatures of dark-matter annihilation, decay or related new physics. Conventional astrophysical sources and propagation can produce similar signals, requiring background modeling; design sensitivity is not a measured limit or discovery.
